To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a wheat PBS1 (TaPBS1) homolog, which harbors the STRPH motif rather than the SEMPH motif of the PBS1, is not recognized by RESISTANCE TO PSUDOMONAS 5 (RPS 5).

the SEMPH motif of PBS1 is important for the association of PBS1 and the recognition of PBS1, while the STRPH motif of the PBS1 homolog in wheat is not required for the association but is important for the recognition.
the “SEMPH motif” of PBS1 plays an important role in its recognition by RPS5 and that the “EM” in the SEMMPH motif is crucial for the function of PBS1.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanism of plant innate immunity, especially the mechanism of the “decoy receptor” in plant innate immunity, which is of great significance to understand the molecular basis of plant resistance to pathogens.
the mechanism of PBS-1 functioning in plant immunity, which will help understand the molecular basis of plant resistance.
the mechanism of PBS 1 functioning in innate immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SEMPH motif in the PBS1 is not required for RPS5 recognition, but is required for the RPS5-mediated signaling pathway.
the SEMPH motif in the PBS1 is required for the recognition by RPS5, but not required for its cleavage by AvrPpbB.
PBS1 is a decoy kinase that is cleaved by AvrpPphB, and that the SEMPH motif in the N terminus is required for RPS5 recognition and HR activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“SEMPH”, not “STRPH”, allows PBS1 to be recognized by RPS5.
the SEMPH motif in the C-terminus of PBS1 is not required for its association with RPS5 but is required for its recognition by RPS5.
“SEMPH”, but not “STRPH” is required for PBS1 to function in RPS5-mediated immunity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SEMPH motif plays a role in the recognition of PBS1 but not the interaction of PBS1 with the receptor RPS5.
the SEMPH motif in Arabidopsis PBS is required for its recognition by RPS5 and the negatively charged amino acid “E” in this motif plays an important role.
the difference between the SEMPH and STRPH motifs points to the importance for the “EM” in the SEM PH motif.
